title: Proper finite-centre pinching of a projective scheme
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $X\to S$ a projective morphism [def-kun-projective]. Let $Z,T$ be finite $S$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:Z\to T$ be a finite surjective $S$-morphism [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Assume that the underlying set $|Z|$ is finite; its points need not be closed in $X$. Then $X/S$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and carries an ample invertible sheaf $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; an affine open $U\subseteq X$ contains $i(Z)$. The pushout $P=X\amalg_ZT$ exists in all schemes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. With its maps $a:X\to P$ and $b:T\to P$, the morphism $P\to S$ is proper and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], $a$ is finite and surjective, $b$ is a closed immersion, the square is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product], and $X\setminus i(Z)\to P\setminus b(T)$ is an isomorphism. The sheaf and simultaneous affine-chart descriptions of the Ferrand square hold: $\mathcal O_P=a_*\mathcal O_X\times_{c_*\mathcal O_Z}b_*\mathcal O_T$, where $c=ai=bj$; on a cover by affine opens $W\subseteq P$, their inverse images in $X,T,Z$ are $\operatorname{Spec}A,\operatorname{Spec}E,\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $A\twoheadrightarrow D$, and $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_D E)$, where $A\times_D E=\{(u,v):u|_D=j^*v\}$ has coordinatewise operations. Every open restriction is again a pushout. Empty $Z,T$ and empty $X$ are allowed whenever the hypotheses hold. No flatness, smoothness, fibre-dimension, or degree-two assumption is made.

source.place: Agent extraction of old steps 1--3: Tags 0E25 (proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral), 0E26 (lemma-pushout-separated), 0E27 (lemma-pushout-finite-type); more-algebra.tex Tag 00IT (lemma-fibre-product-finite-type), generator argument; properties.tex Tag 01ZY (lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine).

proof.text: Choose the finite projective-space embedding supplied by [def-kun-projective]. By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], $X/S$ is proper. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible] to that embedding over the affine base $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$: its restricted twisting sheaf $L$ is an ample invertible sheaf on $X$.

Apply [lem-sc-ample-finite-set-affine] to the finite subset $i(|Z|)$ of $X$ to obtain an affine open $U$ containing it; the lemma does not require its points to be closed. The finite map $j$ is integral by [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft]. Thus every set $i(j^{-1}(\{t\}))$ lies in this same affine open $U$.

Apply [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] to $i,j$ using Step 2. It gives the scheme pushout $P$, its induced structure map to $S$, the integral affine map $a$, the closed immersion $b$, the cartesian square, the displayed structure-sheaf fibre product, the simultaneous affine charts with coordinatewise fibre-product rings, and the pushout property after every open restriction. These are the corresponding clauses of the assertion, with the names $A,E,D$ used there.

source.place: Tag 0E25 (proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral), statement and affine-chart/open-restriction construction in its proof.

proof.text: The quotient-space description in [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] makes $|a(X)|\cup|b(T)|=|P|$. For each $t\in T$, surjectivity of $j$ gives $z\in Z$ with $j(z)=t$, whence $b(t)=a(i(z))$. Therefore $a$ is surjective and $c(Z)=b(T)$ as sets. In the complement isomorphism of that same node, $T\setminus j(Z)$ is empty; it becomes precisely $X\setminus i(Z)\simeq P\setminus b(T)$.

To check finiteness of $a$, take any affine open $W\subseteq P$. Its inverse image in $X$ is affine since $a$ is integral. Its inverse image in $T$ is affine since the closed immersion $b$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc]; its inverse image in $Z$ is then affine since $j$ is finite. The open-restriction and affine-case assertions of [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] identify these rings as $A,E,D$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=A\times_D E$, with $\alpha:A\twoheadrightarrow D$. By the definition of finite morphism, $D$ is a finite $E$-module.

source.place: Tag 0E25 (proposition-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral), affine case and open restriction; morphisms.tex Tag 01WH (definition-integral).

proof.text: Choose $E$-module generators $d_1,\ldots,d_n$ of $D$ and lifts $x_k\in A$ with $\alpha(x_k)=d_k$. For $x\in A$, write $\alpha(x)=\sum_k\beta(e_k)d_k$, where $\beta:E\to D$ is the other structure map, and choose $r_k\in A$ with $\alpha(r_k)=\beta(e_k)$. Then $(r_k,e_k)\in B$ and $h=x-\sum_k r_kx_k\in\ker\alpha$, so $(h,0)\in B$. Hence $x=(h,0)\cdot1+\sum_k(r_k,e_k)\cdot x_k$ for the $B$-action on $A$. Thus $1,x_1,\ldots,x_n$ generate $A$ over $B$. As Step 5 treats every affine $W$, [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] gives finiteness of $a$. The argument includes $D=0$ by taking no $d_k$.

source.place: Tag 00IT (lemma-fibre-product-finite-type), explicit module-generator argument in its proof; only the generator argument, not its Artin--Tate conclusion, is needed here.

proof.text: The one-element affine cover $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ Noetherian shows that $S$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The finite morphisms $T/S$ and $Z/S$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Consequently $X,T$ are separated over $S$ and $X,T,Z$ are locally of finite type over $S$, by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The separatedness and locally-finite-type clauses of [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] now apply to $P/S$. Since $X/S$ is universally closed and $a$ is surjective, [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] says that $P/S$ is proper.

By [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], the locally finite type morphism $P/S$ is locally of finite presentation. Properness gives quasi-compactness by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. These three conditions are exactly finite presentation in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The empty cases require no exception: if $Z$ is empty then surjectivity forces $T$ empty, the pushout is $X$, and the zero affine ring is allowed in the chart calculation. If $X$ is empty, so are $Z,T$, and $P$ is empty as well.

S1: def-kun-projective uses P({0..N};S), the same projective space as lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible over affine Spec R, which gives an ample L; projective-implies-proper gives properness. S2: 01ZY has no closedness hypothesis, so U contains i(Z), which contains every i(j^{-1}(t)); finite implies integral. S3: every clause taken from lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout is in its statement (0E25 situation checked). S4: the quotient topology plus surjectivity of j give a surjective, c(Z)=b(T), and T minus j(Z) empty, hence the complement isomorphism. S5: for any affine W, the preimages under a and b are affine because a and b are affine, and c^{-1}W=j^{-1}(b^{-1}W) is affine because j is finite; the open-restriction and affine-case clauses give W=Spec(A x_D E). S7: Z and T finite hence proper; the Ferrand separatedness clause (0E26) and lft clause (0E27) apply; the image of a universally closed map under surjective a (03GN node) gives P/S proper. S8: lft over a Noetherian base gives lfp; quasi-compact and quasi-separated then give finite presentation.
